source.title: Punishment resistance for cocaine is associated with inflexible habits in rats

confidence_rationale: The one entry that connects the two halves of the argument empirically: it measures habitual control (outcome devaluation) and harm sensitivity (footshock punishment) in the SAME animals and finds them coupled -- punishment resistance tracks continued habitual control, punishment sensitivity tracks a shift back to goal-directed control. That is INV-093's trade with harm as the second axis rather than a devalued reward, which is exactly the inference Dickinson (1985) cannot license on its own. Discounted to 0.65 because the primary preparation is cocaine self-administration, where drug pharmacology is an alternative explanation for both variables, and because the design is correlational across individual differences rather than an experimental sweep of refinement strength.
failure_signatures: Harm sensitivity and habitual control move together in the same individuals: the animals that kept responding under punishment were the ones still under habitual control, so degraded harm sensitivity is not independent of how automatised the behaviour has become.

Punishment-resistant animals showed habitual responding AFTER punishment despite not showing it before, so exposure to the aversive signal drove the behaviour further into automaticity rather than recruiting outcome-sensitive control -- the corrective feedback made the problem worse in exactly the population where it mattered.

The effect appeared in parallel food experiments and differed by sex, so it is neither purely a drug phenomenon nor uniform across individuals -- a mechanism can pass the invariant on average while failing in an identifiable subpopulation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In rats trained to self-administer cocaine and then exposed to random footshock punishment, punishment resistance was associated with continued use of habits whereas punishment sensitivity was associated with increased goal-directed control; punishment-resistant rats showed persistent habitual responding after punishment despite not showing habits beforehand. Parallel food experiments showed the same pattern in males, while females showed habitual responding both before and after punishment. The authors conclude punishment resistance relates to habits that have become inflexible and persist under conditions that should encourage a shift to goal-directed behaviour.
mapping.ree_translation: This closes the inferential gap left by Dickinson (1985). That paper establishes that refinement produces autonomy from outcome VALUE; INV-093 needs autonomy from HARM. Here both are measured in the same animals and they co-vary: the more habitual the control, the less the behaviour bends to an aversive consequence. For REE this means the harm-sensitivity axis of INV-093's panel is not an independent property that a refinement mechanism might happen to leave alone -- it is coupled to the degree of automatisation the refinement produces, so measuring competence and harm sensitivity jointly is measuring two faces of one variable, which is precisely why they cannot be collapsed into one score.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three real limits. (1) The primary preparation is cocaine self-administration, and drug-induced striatal plasticity is an alternative common cause of both punishment resistance and habitual control -- the parallel food experiments mitigate this but are secondary and show a sex difference the cocaine arm does not fully mirror. (2) The design is correlational across individual differences, not an experimental manipulation of refinement strength, so it establishes coupling rather than the direction INV-093 asserts (refinement CAUSING harm-sensitivity loss). (3) Footshock punishment is a crude and exogenous harm signal, quite unlike the endogenous harm and other-agent channels INV-093 is written about; the sibling INV-092 evidence on selective permeability is the better guide to what that channel should look like.
mapping.source_context: Male and female rats; cocaine self-administration training followed by random-footshock punishment; outcome-devaluation tests of goal-directed versus habitual control administered before and after punishment testing; parallel food-reinforced experiments run alongside.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.70: a careful within-animal design measuring both variables with adequate sex balance and a food control, in a young specialist journal, single-lab and not yet replicated. Mapping fidelity 0.70: the coupling of habitual control to punishment insensitivity is exactly the relation INV-093 needs, but measured correlationally rather than as a refinement sweep. Transfer risk 0.50, the highest here alongside the Safety Gym entry: an addiction preparation carries a pharmacological confound that has no REE analogue at all, and reading a drug-seeking result as a general statement about skill refinement requires the food arm to carry more weight than its secondary status supports.
